public_rationale: On March 15, 2023, OpenAI's chief scientist confirmed that OpenAI did not disclose GPT-4's parameter count or training data [e1]. The original technical report described GPT-4 as Transformer-based, providing a general architecture label [e2]. These disclosures support the reading that specific technical details were withheld, while qualifying any broader suggestion that nothing about the model was public [e1, e2].
limitations: The supplied excerpts do not directly establish the disclosure status of every listed category, particularly training energy and processor count.
Withheld compute details would not by themselves establish withheld electricity consumption; a hardware description would not establish processor count.
The March 15 sources do not establish their precise publication order relative to Marcus's post.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has not disclosed GPT-4's size, architecture, energy use, processor count, or training data.

statement.excerpt: We don’t know how big it is; we don’t know what the architecture is, we don’t know how much energy was used; we don’t how many processors were used; we don’t know what it was trained on etc.

from_speaker: We don’t know how big it is
we don’t know what the architecture is
we don’t know how much energy was used
we don’t how many processors were used
we don’t know what it was trained on
our_interpretation: We means the public research community, not OpenAI's own employees.
The plain reading concerns GPT-4's specific technical specifications: parameter count, detailed architecture, training energy consumption, processor count, and identifiable training-data composition.
A general model-family label or broad description of data sources does not disclose those specifications.
The target is the disclosure record at launch and publication, March 14–15, 2023. Later disclosures cannot change what was public then.
criteria.support_condition: The release materials and contemporaneous statements establish that the listed specific technical details were withheld from the public.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Publicly available materials by publication disclose the listed specifications. Disclosure of only some would qualify the claim rather than refute all of it.

evidence.excerpt: And the reason we don’t disclose the training data is pretty much the same reason we don’t disclose the number of parameters.
evidence.locator: Sutskever's response to the question about training data and legal liability
evidence.explanation: Sutskever directly confirms withholding size and training data. The article also documents the absent energy and hardware information and reproduces OpenAI's statement withholding architectural and training details.
